new.title: Step into the Baroque hall of the Abbey Library
new.desc: The Abbey Library of St. Gallen holds about 170,000 manuscripts, documents and prints, among them some of Europe's oldest. Its Baroque hall, finished in the 18th century, is part of the UNESCO-listed abbey precinct.
new.tip: Visitors pull on large woollen slippers over their shoes and photography is not allowed. Allow 30 to 45 minutes and check the official site for current admission.
new.q: Stiftsbibliothek St. Gallen, Klosterhof 6d, St. Gallen

new.title: Admire the twin towers of St. Gallen Cathedral
new.desc: The Baroque cathedral stands at the heart of the UNESCO abbey precinct and succeeds the monastery church of the Abbey of St Gall. Its richly decorated interior is among the major Baroque church spaces of Switzerland.
new.tip: Entry to the church is free. Guided tours are offered on selected Saturdays at 10:30, so check dom.kathsg.ch.
new.q: Kathedrale St. Gallen, Klosterhof, St. Gallen

new.title: See embroidery and lace at the Textile Museum
new.desc: The Textilmuseum sits in the Palazzo Rosso at Vadianstrasse 2 and has been based there since 1886. It documents the embroidery and lace industry that made St. Gallen rich, with fabrics, sample books and costumes.
new.tip: Adult admission is about CHF 12 and it is usually open 10:00 to 17:00; verify on textilmuseum.ch.
new.q: Textilmuseum St. Gallen, Vadianstrasse 2, St. Gallen

new.title: Walk through Pipilotti Rist's red Stadtlounge
new.desc: The Stadtlounge, called Red Square by locals, is a red-tinted public living room by artist Pipilotti Rist and architect Carlos Martinez. It covers a plaza in the Bleicheli quarter around Raiffeisenplatz.
new.tip: Free and open all day. The sofa-like street furniture invites you to sit, and it is nicest in good light.
new.q: Roter Platz Stadtlounge, Raiffeisenplatz, Bleichestrasse, St. Gallen

new.title: Visit the reformed church of St. Laurenzen
new.desc: St. Laurenzen is the Protestant parish church of the city, with a neo-Gothic tower rebuilt in the 19th century that keeps parts of the older tower finished in 1423. The tower can be climbed on guided visits for views over the old town and abbey precinct.
new.tip: Tower visits are offered in the warmer months and may be closed in winter. Confirm times with the parish.
new.q: Kirche St. Laurenzen, Marktplatz, St. Gallen

new.title: Browse the Kunstmuseum in the Stadtpark
new.desc: The Kunstmuseum St. Gallen at Museumstrasse 32 is the largest art collection in eastern Switzerland, running from the late Middle Ages to the present with works from Dutch painters to Monet and Hodler. It stands in the Stadtpark.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00, Thursday until 20:00. Combine with a stroll in the park.
new.q: Kunstmuseum St. Gallen, Museumstrasse 32, St. Gallen

new.title: Trace local history at the Kulturmuseum
new.desc: The Kulturmuseum St. Gallen, formerly the Historisches und Völkerkundemuseum, occupies a neoclassical building opened in 1921. It holds some 70,000 objects of regional history and ethnology, including the carved camel from the Kamelerker.
new.tip: Open most days 10:00 to 17:00, Wednesday until 19:00, though times may have changed; check kulturmuseumsg.ch.
new.q: Kulturmuseum St. Gallen, Museumstrasse 50, St. Gallen

new.title: Meet a dinosaur at the Naturmuseum St. Gallen
new.desc: The Naturmuseum at Rorschacher Strasse 263 opened in a new building in 2016 and is known for Switzerland's largest landscape relief of St. Gallen and Appenzell. Its star exhibit is a fossilised duck-billed dinosaur skeleton.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00, Wednesday until 20:00. It stands next to the Botanical Garden.
new.q: Naturmuseum St. Gallen, Rorschacher Strasse 263, St. Gallen

new.title: Wander the greenhouses of the Botanical Garden
new.desc: The municipal Botanischer Garten at Stephanshornstrasse 4 shows about 8,000 labelled plants in open beds and several greenhouses. Admission is free.
new.tip: Outdoor area and tropical house open daily 8:00 to 17:00 with a midday break for the tropical house.
new.q: Botanischer Garten St. Gallen, Stephanshornstrasse 4, St. Gallen

new.title: Look up at the Kamelerker on Spisergasse
new.desc: The Kamelerker is the best-known of the old town's many oriel windows; its lower part dates from 1673. It takes its name from carved camels, now kept in the Kulturmuseum. Around 100 oriels survive in the city.
new.tip: Free. Look up at first-floor level and also find the Sternenerker at Spisergasse 19 from 1699.

new.title: Climb Freudenberg for views of the Alpstein
new.desc: The Freudenberg is the local hill above Drei Weieren, with a panoramic path and benches. In clear weather the view takes in St. Gallen, the Alpstein and Lake Constance.
new.tip: Reached on footpaths from the Drei Weieren area. Fire pits make it a popular picnic spot.

new.title: Explore the Lokremise railway depot arts centre
new.desc: The Lokremise is a former locomotive depot built between 1903 and 1911, now a cultural centre with theatre, dance, art and the Kinok cinema. Its art space is run with the Kunstmuseum St. Gallen.
new.tip: Check lokremise.ch for the programme; the Kinok shows independent films at Grünbergstrasse 7.
new.q: Lokremise St. Gallen, Grünbergstrasse 7, St. Gallen

new.title: See young art at Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen
new.desc: Founded in 1985, the Kunst Halle at Davidstrasse 40 shows contemporary art in four to five exhibitions a year. It counts among Switzerland's key institutions for young art.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Friday 12:00 to 18:00 and weekends 11:00 to 17:00 only during exhibitions; check the site first. Admission about CHF 7.
new.q: Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen, Davidstrasse 40, St. Gallen

new.title: Browse the art library at Sitterwerk
new.desc: The Sitterwerk foundation occupies a former textile dye works on Sittertalstrasse and combines an art library with a material archive and the neighbouring Kunstgiesserei foundry. Books carry sensors so any shelf placement can be tracked.
new.tip: Open Monday to Friday 9:00 to 17:00 and Sunday 14:00 to 18:00. Closed Saturdays.

new.title: Eat bratwurst with rösti at Zum Bäumli
new.desc: Zum Bäumli is a small first-floor Erststockbeizli on Schmiedgasse, one of the old town's traditional timber-framed taverns. Reviewers praise its bratwurst with rösti and onion sauce at friendly prices.
new.tip: The St. Gallen bratwurst is traditionally eaten without mustard. Check opening days before going.

new.title: Grab an OLMA-Bratwurst at Gemperli
new.desc: The Gemperli takeaway on Schmiedgasse has grilled OLMA-Bratwurst and Schüblig since the 1940s. Since 2021 it also operates as Bratwurst & Bowls with poke bowls beside the traditional sausages.
new.tip: Eat the sausage standing up with a Bürli roll and skip the mustard. Try the Schüblig too.
new.q: Metzgerei Gemperli Bratwurst & Bowls, Schmiedgasse 34, St. Gallen

new.title: Order the veal bratwurst at Zum Goldenen Schäfli
new.desc: Housed in the former butchers' guildhall at Metzgergasse 5, the building dates to around 1484 and was saved from demolition in the 1970s by a citizens' cooperative. It is the best-known Erststockbeizli, with uneven floors and ceiling.
new.tip: The St. Gallen veal bratwurst with onion sauce is the dish to order. Book ahead for evenings.
new.q: Zum Goldenen Schäfli, Metzgergasse 5, St. Gallen

new.title: Buy a St. Galler Biber at Confiserie Roggwiller
new.desc: Confiserie Roggwiller on Multergasse is the best-known source of St. Galler Biber, a honey-spiced cake with a sweet almond filling. The recipe goes back to around 1800 and the shop dates from 1941.
new.tip: Buy a slice to take home or sit in the tea room. Confirm opening hours as directory listings conflict.

new.title: Share small plates at Restaurant Neubad
new.desc: Neubad sits at Bankgasse 6 in a historic Erststockbeizli building from around 1550. It serves seasonal, regionally inspired small plates with a modern touch.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Saturday for lunch from 11:30 and dinner from 17:30. Call +41 71 222 86 83 to reserve.

new.title: Drink fresh Schützengarten beer at Brauwerk
new.desc: Restaurant Brauwerk at Bahnhofstrasse 19 is a small brewery, restaurant and bar by the main station and home of the experimental brewers of Schützengarten. Schützengarten calls itself Switzerland's oldest brewery, with roots in the monks of St. Gallen.
new.tip: Open Monday to Saturday from 11:30; lunch menus start around CHF 20. Try the house-brewed specials.

new.title: Dine at Zum Schwarzen Adler on the Marktplatz
new.desc: Zum Schwarzen Adler is an Erststockbeizli at Marktplatz 12 in a house over 300 years old. It has a first-floor dining room and a summer terrace in the heart of the old town.
new.tip: Hours vary and weekends may be groups only. Phone +41 71 222 75 07 before visiting.
new.q: Zum Schwarzen Adler, Marktplatz 12, St. Gallen

new.title: Settle into the Kaffeehaus on Linsebühlstrasse
new.desc: Kaffeehaus at Linsebühlstrasse 77 is a classic café with traditional charm just outside the old town core. It suits a quiet coffee and comfortable seating.
new.tip: Listed hours are Tuesday to Friday 8:00 to 18:00; check before going.

new.title: Swim at the Drei Weieren ponds
new.desc: The three ponds were created around 1610 to secure the textile bleaching and fire-fighting water supply and are now a favourite bathing area with historic bathhouses. They sit above the old town in a protected landscape.
new.tip: Walk up in about 20 minutes or take the Mühleggbahn. Swimming is in summer only.

new.title: Watch ibex at Wildpark Peter und Paul
new.desc: Founded in 1892 by the Diana hunting association, the wildlife park on Rotmonten is known for its ibex cliffs. Young ibex were bought in 1910 for the Swiss reintroduction programme.
new.tip: Entry is free and the park is open around the clock. Parking is limited, so go by public transport.
new.q: Wildpark Peter und Paul, Kirchlistrasse 92, St. Gallen

new.title: Ride the Mühleggbahn funicular to the ponds
new.desc: The Mühleggbahn links the old town with St. Georgen and the Drei Weieren area. It began in 1893 as a water-counterweight railway and was rebuilt in 2004; the ride takes about 90 seconds.
new.tip: Run by the city transport company. Combine it with a walk to the ponds.

new.title: Hike the St. Galler Brückenweg to the Sitter viaducts
new.desc: The bridge trail follows the Sitter gorge from Haggen to Spisegg past the 365 m Bodensee-Toggenburg-Bahn viaduct, built 1907 to 1910, and the SBB viaduct. Information boards stand at each bridge.
new.tip: About 8 km and 2 hours 15 minutes, March to November. Return by bus or S-Bahn.

new.title: Stroll the Christmas market under the Sternenstadt
new.desc: The Advent market runs through Waaghaus, Bohl, Marktgasse and Neugasse while some 700 LED stars light the old town. The 2025 market ran from 27 November to 24 December.
new.tip: Visit after dusk for the lights; some stars are failing, so fewer may shine.

new.title: Join the OLMA autumn fair and its Bratwurst
new.desc: OLMA is Switzerland's largest consumer fair for agriculture and food, held in St. Gallen for eleven days each October. The 83rd edition was set to open on 8 October 2026.
new.tip: Eat the OLMA-Bratwurst here and expect large crowds. Check olma-messen.ch for dates.
new.q: OLMA Messen St. Gallen, Splügenstrasse 12, St. Gallen

new.title: Shop the Marktplatz weekly market
new.desc: A fresh-produce market takes place on the Marktplatz, organised by Verein Marktfrisch, on Saturdays from 9:00 to 15:00 and reportedly Wednesdays too.
new.tip: Check the schedule since the square is under redesign.

new.title: Hear the Sinfonieorchester in the Tonhalle
new.desc: The Tonhalle is the concert hall of Konzert und Theater St. Gallen, where the Sinfonieorchester St. Gallen plays its series of evening, lunch and family concerts.
new.tip: Programme and tickets at konzertundtheater.ch.
new.q: Tonhalle St. Gallen, Museumstrasse 25, St. Gallen

new.title: Stroll the painted houses of Appenzell Hauptgasse
new.desc: The pedestrian Hauptgasse of Appenzell village is lined with painted wooden houses with curved gables, many rebuilt after the fire of 1560. The village centre and Landsgemeindeplatz are car-free.
new.tip: Public village tours run in summer. Many bakeries along the street sell Biber.

new.title: Learn Appenzell traditions at Museum Appenzell
new.desc: Museum Appenzell at Hauptgasse 4 covers the folk culture of Innerrhoden, with hand embroidery, furniture painting, tourism and popular piety. It has a large photo collection.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; hours differ by season. Admission about CHF 7 to 9.

new.title: Ride up Ebenalp and walk into the Wildkirchli caves
new.desc: The cable car from Wasserauen climbs 723 m in six minutes to the Ebenalp. A short walk leads to the Wildkirchli caves, with an altar cave made a chapel in 1657 and a hermit's cellar cave.
new.tip: Cable car runs year-round roughly every 15 minutes. Allow about 15 minutes to the caves.

new.title: Have rösti at Berggasthaus Äscher on the cliff
new.desc: The Berggasthaus Äscher-Wildkirchli clings to a rock face and has served hikers since 1846. It is one of the oldest mountain inns in Switzerland.
new.tip: Open May to November, from 7:30. Walk about 15 minutes from Ebenalp through the caves.

new.title: Walk from Wasserauen to Seealpsee
new.desc: The Seealpsee is an Alpstein lake reached on a roughly 3 km paved track from Wasserauen. Two mountain inns stand at the shore, including Berggasthaus Forelle, known for trout.
new.tip: About 1 to 2 hours each way. Inns open roughly May to October.

new.title: Reach the summit of Säntis at 2,502 m
new.desc: The Säntis is the highest peak of the Alpstein, with views on clear days over six countries. A cable car runs from Schwägalp in about ten minutes and the summit has a restaurant.
new.tip: The cable car was modernised in 2026 with the summit reachable only on foot in summer; check saentisbahn.ch for current status.

new.title: Dine at the revolving restaurant on Hoher Kasten
new.desc: A cable car from Brülisau rises in eight minutes to 1,794 m and the only revolving restaurant in eastern Switzerland. The summit looks over the Rhine valley and Alpstein.
new.tip: Operates April through February. Children up to 15 ride free.

new.title: Watch Appenzeller cheese made at the Schaukäserei
new.desc: The Appenzeller Schaukäserei in Stein AR lets visitors look into the cheese vats; its cellar holds up to 12,500 wheels. There is a shop, restaurant and herbal blending.
new.tip: Public tours Wednesday and Sunday at 14:00. Admission about CHF 12.

new.title: Meet the Silvesterchläuse at the Urnäsch museum
new.desc: The Appenzeller Brauchtumsmuseum in a house over 400 years old focuses on the Silvesterchlausen tradition, with masks and bonnets, alpine cattle drives and string music.
new.tip: Winter hours are limited. Phone +41 71 364 23 22 or check museum-urnaesch.ch.

new.title: Tour the Brauquöll visitor centre at Locher brewery
new.desc: The Brauerei Locher visitor centre Brauquöll opened in April 2024 with an audio-guided tour, a film in the historic hops cellar and a small museum.
new.tip: Public tastings cost CHF 14 for ages 16 and over; check days. The brewery is at Brauereiplatz 1.

new.title: Buy Appenzeller Biber at Drei Könige
new.desc: The Drei Könige bakery at Hauptgasse 24 to 26 is named as a place to buy Appenzeller Biber and Biberli, the spiced honey-bread speciality.
new.tip: Compare the Biber with the St. Gallen version.

new.title: Hike the Gäbris ridge above Gais
new.desc: The Gäbris, at 1,251 m, is the northernmost pre-Alpine peak of Switzerland with views over the Rhine valley and Alpstein. A circuit of about 7.5 km leads from Landmark via two guesthouses to Gais.
new.tip: About 2 hours 10 minutes, March to October.

new.title: Visit Rapperswil Castle and its rose garden
new.desc: Schloss Rapperswil dates from the 13th century and overlooks Lake Zurich, housing the Polish Museum and a restaurant. Below it lies the Rosengarten with over 15,000 roses.
new.tip: Roses peak around late June.

new.title: Cross Lake Zurich on the Rapperswil-Hurden Holzsteg
new.desc: The wooden footbridge across the upper lake is about 841 m long, stands on 233 piles and opened in April 2001. A medieval crossing existed from 1358 to 1878.
new.tip: Free to walk and open all day.

new.title: Take a boat across the Walensee
new.desc: Boats run from Unterterzen or Murg to Quinten year-round, and Weesen to Walenstadt in season. The Walensee is deep blue and rimmed by steep cliffs.
new.tip: Timetables differ by season; see Walensee Schifffahrt.

new.title: Eat lake fish at Seehus in Quinten
new.desc: Quinten is a car-free wine village reachable only by boat or on foot. Restaurant Seehus sits on the shore and leans on fish.
new.tip: Takes a winter break from November and is closed Monday and Tuesday.

new.title: Hike the Flumserberg Prodalp and Tannenboden
new.desc: Flumserberg is reached by gondola from Unterterzen and has summer trails, a culinary Panorama-Route hike and winter walking trails around Tannenbodenalp and Prodalp.
new.tip: Winter trails can close for avalanche risk.

new.title: Lunch at the Herzog & de Meuron Chäserrugg restaurant
new.desc: The summit restaurant at Chäserrugg in the Toggenburg was rebuilt by Herzog & de Meuron in a plain timber style at about 2,262 m, with views over six countries.
new.tip: Summer hours around 9:00 to 17:00; check chaeserrugg.ch.

new.title: Walk the Tamina Gorge to Altes Bad Pfäfers
new.desc: The trail from Bad Ragaz leads through the Tamina Gorge to the Old Pfäfers Bath, the oldest preserved Baroque thermal bath in Switzerland, where a 36.5 C spring is reached by a 450 m path.
new.tip: The area is car-free. Many walks end with a soak in Tamina Therme.

new.title: See the Kornhaus on Rorschach harbour
new.desc: The Kornhaus was built in 1746 to 1749 by Caspar Bagnato for the St. Gallen abbot and houses the Museum im Kornhaus since 2011. Ships sail from the harbour to Lindau and Mainau.
new.tip: Stroll the Seepromenade afterwards.

new.title: Visit Zwingli's birthplace in Wildhaus
new.desc: The reformer Huldrych Zwingli was born in 1484 in this timber house of 1449, one of the oldest wooden houses in Switzerland, now a memorial museum since 1910.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 14:00 to 16:00 from Christmas to Easter and Whitsun to mid-October.

new.title: Walk Wil's old town and the Hof
new.desc: Wil's old town is anchored by the Hof zu Wil, which the Count of Toggenburg left to the monastery of St. Gallen in 1226. It won the Wakker Prize for its preservation.
new.tip: The Stadtmuseum is in the Hof; tourist office at Marktgasse 62.
new.q: Hof zu Wil, Marktgasse, Wil SG

new.title: Explore Arbon Castle and the old town
new.desc: Schloss Arbon was built in 1515 to 1520 for the Bishop of Constance on a Roman fort and houses the Historical Museum. The old town lies on a headland jutting into Lake Constance.
new.tip: A lakeside promenade over 3 km runs beside the town.

new.title: See old trucks at the Saurer Museum in Arbon
new.desc: The volunteer-run Saurer Museum in the former factory at Weitegasse 8 shows commercial vehicles, post buses, fire engines, engines and textile machines.
new.tip: Staff on site the first weekend of each month; check hours.

new.title: Take a harbour tour in Romanshorn
new.desc: Romanshorn has the largest harbour on Lake Constance by water area. The Museum am Hafen in the old customs house at Hafenstrasse 31 covers railways, shipping and ferry traffic.
new.tip: Museum open Sunday 14:00 to 17:00. Harbour cruises depart in season.

new.title: Walk the Seeburgpark lakeshore in Kreuzlingen
new.desc: The park is about 2.5 km long with direct lake access, ponds of national importance, a petting zoo, adventure playground and 19-hole minigolf, beside Seeburg castle.
new.tip: The Seemuseum is in an old grain barn here. Nearest station Kreuzlingen Hafen.

new.title: Climb Schloss Frauenfeld and its Thurgau museum
new.desc: The medieval castle with a keep has housed the Historisches Museum Thurgau since 1960, covering late medieval Thurgau on three floors.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 13:00 to 17:00; check the site.

new.title: Lunch at Kartause Ittingen's Restaurant Mühle
new.desc: The former Carthusian monastery near Warth runs Restaurant Mühle in its mill with a wheel of 1870 and a garden restaurant. Menus use produce from its own farm, dairy, butchery and wine cellar.
new.tip: Open daily 8:30 to 22:30, warm food until 20:30. Phone +41 52 748 44 11.

new.title: Tour Napoleon III's Arenenberg estate
new.desc: Schloss Arenenberg in Salenstein was the home of Queen Hortense from 1817 and where Napoleon III grew up. The Napoleonmuseum shows restored rooms, and a neo-Gothic chapel from 1832 stands in the grounds.
new.tip: Admission CHF 15; check seasonal hours.

new.title: Cross the Alte Thurbrücke into Bischofszell
new.desc: The eight-arched old Thur bridge finished in 1487 is nicknamed Krumme Brücke for its kinks and is a major late medieval bridge. The old town won the Wakker Prize in 1987.
new.tip: Free to walk.
